heading: More training samples can raise test error near the interpolation threshold
definition: near the interpolation threshold, increasing the number of training samples can raise test error.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce the effect in linear regression and synthetic neural models under specific conditions. Evidence in language models remains limited, especially for locating the rise near interpolation.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 for toy/classical and synthetic neural settings, mostly with parameter-count size not stated. R0 for the identified <1B FineWeb language-model setting. At 1–10B, R0 for more-data loss increases alone and ? for their location near interpolation. No V3 coverage at 10–100B or >100B.
suggested_status.reason: Non-original studies reproduce conditional sample-wise harm in linear regression and trained attention models: arXiv:2605.27989#reg-noise03-n115, arXiv:2605.27989#reg-noise03-n128, arXiv:2405.11751#R4, arXiv:2405.11751#R5 and arXiv:2405.11751#R6. This supports provisional R2 for the existential claim in these settings. The tied ReLU autoencoder sweep in arXiv:2605.27989#toy-n100, arXiv:2605.27989#toy-n200 and arXiv:2605.27989#toy-n500 establishes harmful sample increases without identifying the peak with exact interpolation; its V3 verdict is limits_scope and it does not supply threshold-localized replication evidence. Scale-specific evidence remains narrower: arXiv:2505.24832#r5, arXiv:2505.24832#r6, arXiv:2505.24832#r7 and arXiv:2505.24832#r8 report figure-only FineWeb behavior, while arXiv:2307.06290#r2 and arXiv:2307.06290#r3 report 7B instruction-tuning loss increases without a measured interpolation threshold. counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size and versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size contain <1B and 1-10B coverage but no larger buckets. Monotonic results and local artifacts constrain conditions rather than establishing failure of every instance of this existential claim.
suggested_status.open_questions: Replicated sample-size sweeps with training interpolation explicitly measured, uncertainty on the harmful interval, matched tuning and training budgets, and held-out metrics would clarify the neural and language-model scope. Threshold-localized instruction-tuning tests and tests above 10B would change the scale-specific assessment.

source.title: Deep double descent: where bigger models and more data hurt
source.authors: Preetum Nakkiran; Gal Kaplun; Yamini Bansal; Tristan Yang; B. Barak; I. Sutskever

original_result.setup: The original study varied training-set size for two Transformer sizes on IWSLT'14.
original_result.result: Comparisons of 4K and 18K samples showed a regime where more samples increased test loss for both model sizes; numerical losses were reported only in figures. With optimal early stopping, more samples were always better.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

wording_issues.issue: Some harmful-data regions occur away from nominal interpolation or have no interpolation mechanism identified: structured-data neural-network regions, shifted ridge/mixture peaks and medium- or strong-adversary effects. The tied-ReLU sweep establishes harmful sample increases with nonzero training loss, but proximity to interpolation remains unestablished; it is partial evidence for V3 and qualifies its location clause. Nonzero training loss alone does not establish distance from a threshold. Weak-adversary regimes leave the threshold condition untested.

The measured outcome changes the finding. Physical hinge loss peaks while classification error improves. DeepONet endpoint loss and best checkpoint loss differ. Instruction-tuning inference loss and benchmark scores can move differently. Basis Pursuit reports model error rather than held-out prediction error.

wording_issues.phrase: increasing the number of training samples
wording_issues.issue: Artificial zero-response observations, precomputed augmentation, sensor-count increases and fresh-noise repeats or dataset mixtures are distinct interventions. Appending zero-response artificial observations after n0=5 leaves harm from adding genuine training samples cannot_determine. Sensor sweeps hold training snapshots fixed and do not test V3; their training-sample effect is cannot_determine. These cases supply coverage distinctions, not V3 support or scope limitations. The repeated-CIFAR experiment uses independent fresh noise and reports figure-only test errors; at least 200 trials is not established specifically for Figure 7. Sampling schemes should retain their definitions.

The H-SVR threshold is a feasibility boundary. Small-initialization ReLU experiments use an optimization-dependent loss-of-interpolation transition below nominal parameter count. Fixed-feature studies may use matrix rank or invertibility. These definitions should remain study-specific.

The existential wording fits conditional evidence. It does not imply a rise for every learner, sampling design or tuning choice. With σ=1 and β=1, asymptotic H-SVR risk decreases when ε minimizes risk at each δ; S-SVR risk decreases with δ under optimal C at ε=0.6. These are absent harmful-sample effects for V3; peak removal supports V6. Bayes-optimal prediction and well-conditioned Fourier sampling improve through their relevant transitions.

A sample-size plot or unspecified double-descent description does not itself establish a harmful interval near interpolation. Verdict fixes leave the cited ResNet, MNIST random-feature and random-feature regression evidence indeterminate.

method_sensitivity.what: Weakly regularized estimators can have harmful sample intervals. Optimal ridge tuning gives non-increasing MSE with sample size under the stated assumptions. Empirical ridge selection over a finite grid mitigates peaks without establishing disappearance under actual-risk-optimal tuning. With optimal C, S-SVR risk decreases with δ at β=1, σ=1 and ε=0.6, so the harmful sample effect is absent. Stronger quantum-kernel ridge demonstrates suppression rather than uniform disappearance.

method_sensitivity.factor: Label noise, effective noise and realizability
method_sensitivity.what: Removing noise eliminates the Gaussian minimum-norm peak. In Bayesian linear models, noiseless LR is monotone, and the trainable NN equals that monotone curve at matched prior σ=1 and noise η=0. For general noiseless NN priors, absence of sample-wise divergence does not establish absence of every harmful sample increase. Bottlenecked random features can still diverge without noise. Noiseless nonlinear or out-of-RKHS targets can retain peaks. Lower noise can remove quadratic-network double descent.

Spectral gaps change peak visibility and multiplicity. Covariance structure and target alignment can create harmful sample regions away from nominal interpolation. In arXiv:2305.14689, shifted peaks under ridge or mixture structure qualify peak location, whereas full-dimensional MNIST explicitly lacks double descent. Removing small singular values or changing test-feature geometry eliminates linear-regression spikes. Monotone CIFAR10 NTK curves do not establish a V3 scope limitation because coverage near interpolation is unestablished.

Logistic-data classification has harmful sample comparisons under square-loss GD with linear features: at p≈0.5d, error is lowest for n=d/5 and largest for n=3d/5 among d/5, 2d/5 and 3d/5. Under logistic-loss GD with polynomial features, γ=2 and r=5, error at p≈0.4d is lowest for n=d/3 and highest for n=d. With logistic loss, linear features and r=5, larger n improves performance at every model size across n=d/3, 2d/3 and d. Logistic loss also attenuates random-feature peaks. The low-regularization hinge-loss cusp leaves V3 cannot_determine: neither a harmful increasing interval nor its absence or attenuation is established.

The original Transformer baseline reports that optimal early stopping makes additional samples beneficial. Random-feature sample-wise descents develop after sufficient training time. Pendulum DeepONet harm appears under average endpoint loss but is not significant under best loss over iterations.

method_sensitivity.factor: Augmentation, ensemble heterogeneity and subsample selection
method_sensitivity.what: Precomputed augmentation shifts and suppresses the peak as augmentation increases, while augmented empirical risk minimization is monotonic. Heterogeneous feature allocation reduces ensemble peaks; Imagewoof monotonicity is reported for sufficiently high k, including k=16 and k=32. For ridgeless subagging and splagging, oracle subsample-optimized limiting risk F(φ) is nondecreasing in φ. Under Assumptions 1–5 with CEN=MOM, cross-validation gives only (R_CV−F(φ))_+→0 in probability; actual CV-risk monotonicity is cannot_determine from that theorem alone. Exact convergence requires Remark 4.3's stronger uniform assumptions. The subsample-optimized full ridgeless ensemble also has limiting risk monotonically increasing in φ, so harmful sample increases are absent for that optimized risk.

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation metric and physical training protocol
method_sensitivity.what: Physical classification error is monotonic while hinge loss peaks. Without overclamping, the peak is absent or unconvincing, but other conditions also differ. GNN accuracy can lack clear double descent while nonmonotonic test risk establishes more-labels-hurt behavior; interpolation proximity is unestablished for that appendix comparison. The accuracy result does not establish absence or attenuation of harmful sample effects in risk. Instruction-tuning losses and downstream benchmark scores can move differently.

In arXiv:2204.02488, likelihood-weighted acquisition avoids the DeepONet error rise seen with US or LHS. Equidistant and small-jitter Fourier sampling give declining risk through the transition. In arXiv:2208.13080, GP peak severity changes with target-map nonlinearity and associated heavy tails; that study's standard DNN training uses LHS samples and supplies no US acquisition comparison.

Bayesian random-feature bottlenecks permit noise-free divergence absent from trainable deep linear networks. For the latter, absence of divergence alone leaves broader harmful sample increases cannot_determine; monotonicity is established for the matched-prior control σ=1, η=0, which equals noiseless LR. Skip connections dampen linear-denoiser peaks. Nonlinear-autoencoder curves vary with contamination, SNR and domain shift. MNIST feature-map choice and Fashion-MNIST feature-training stage change learning curves and their invertibility thresholds.

Low-dimensional robust models change from beneficial to harmful sample effects as adversary strength increases; interpolation-threshold location is untested, so weak-adversary improvement does not establish a V3 scope limitation. Other well-specified robust minimax and hinge-loss models improve monotonically across their reported adversary settings. For arXiv:2010.11213, standard accuracy increases with n/d across the separability threshold, challenging V3 in those settings. For 10.1109/tnnls.2023.3290592, Figure 1's sampling-ratio δ-axis ticks span 0–6; the exact sampled grid and individual attack budgets are unstated. Loss, dimensionality and regularization differ.
